council: Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead
current_evidence: The council's 'What to submit with your planning application' page links this PDF as 'National and local validation requirements policy: March 2026' and says the Council 'formally adopted the National and Local Validation Requirements on Thursday 5 February 2026'. The PDF cover reads 'Adopted 05.02.2026'.

issues.detail: List date 2026-03-01 is taken from the URL upload path. The document and web page give an adoption date of 5 February 2026; the PDF is labelled March 2026.
issues.evidence: Cover 'Adopted 05.02.2026'; web page 'formally adopted ... on Thursday 5 February 2026'.

issues.detail: These local plan, statement, transport and landscape requirements are not captured: Street Scene Elevations (all major and minor development fronting a highway); Site Levels and Finished Floor Levels (all majors; land not reasonably level; Flood Zones 2/3; swimming pools and basements); Cross Sections (majors; level changes; engineering works; all basements); Phasing Plan (over 50 dwellings; self-build of more than one unit); Marketing Exercise (loss of a protected use under BLP ED3/QP5/TR7/IF6, 12 months' marketing); Financial Viability Assessment (where the HO3 affordable housing requirement is not met); Retail Impact Assessment (retail/leisure over 2,500 sqm, or out-of-centre retail/leisure/office); Rural Workers Needs Assessment (agricultural dwellings in countryside/Green Belt); CEMP (major residential and commercial, including change of use); Parking Management Plan (all majors; some minors and changes of use); Delivery and Servicing Management Plan (majors in town centres); Demolition Method Statement (demolition prior approvals; demolition close to highway or homes); Waste Management, Storage and Collection Strategy (all new residential excluding replacement dwellings; commercial); Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment (over 50 dwellings; non-residential in Green Belt/countryside; tall buildings); Landscaping Scheme (major and minor, excluding change of use).
issues.evidence: Plans (pp.14-17), Statements/Assessments (pp.18-20), Transport (pp.21-23), Trees, Landscape and Ecology (pp.23-26) sections of the PDF.

issues.detail: These environmental and other local requirements are not captured: Air Quality Assessment incl. Emissions Mitigation Assessment (major applications); Contaminated Land Assessment (contamination suspected); Noise Assessment (sensitive uses near noise sources; noise-generating proposals such as plant); Pollution Assessment; Ventilation/Extraction Details (restaurants, pubs, takeaways; plant, air conditioning and air source heat pumps); Crime Prevention Statement (major); Drainage Assessment / SuDS Strategy (all new and replacement dwellings; major non-residential); Sustainability/Energy Statement (new dwellings including conversions and replacements; commercial over 100 sqm); Archaeological Desk Based Assessment (Area of High Archaeological Potential or over 0.4 ha); Structural Survey (substantial demolition with change of use; significant works to listed building fabric; prior approval to residential); Telecommunications Report; Utilities Assessment (all majors).
issues.evidence: Environmental Protection (pp.26-29) and Other Documents (pp.29-32) sections of the PDF.

issues.detail: The 'Other application types' section sets local requirements, yet these rows are '(none)': Change of use - prior approval (GPDO Part 2 Class A larger home extensions: written description with dimensions, site plan, adjoining addresses; Class AA additional storeys: scaled plans and elevations; Parts 3, 4, 6, 11, 16, 20 with class-specific documents such as FRA, transport, noise and contamination for Part 3); Non-material amendment (approved vs proposed comparison plans, supporting statement); Discharge of conditions (information required by the condition); Works to trees (sketch map, tree type and condition, accurate pruning specification; percentage reductions not accepted); S106 modification (obligation to be changed, reasons, land interest, map).
issues.evidence: PDF pp.40-42 'Other Application Types' local list.

issues.detail: Householder has only a Tree survey row, but other local items explicitly apply to householder or to typical householder works: Habitats Survey / Ecology Report ('All applications, including householder'); CIL form ('Always'); Site levels / FFL and Cross sections for basements and swimming pools and for land that is not level; Ventilation/Extraction details for air source heat pumps and air conditioning.
issues.evidence: Habitats Survey/Ecology Report - application types 'All applications, including householder'.

issues.detail: The Ecological Survey trigger excerpt comes from the Demolition Method Statement and Waste storage items ('safeguard trees/protected species and habitats affected by the demolition ... storage and collection of recycling and refuse'). The real trigger is where protected species may be affected or the site is within or abuts a designated nature conservation site, and it applies to all applications including householder.
issues.evidence: Habitats Survey/Ecology Report, BLP Policy NR2.

issues.detail: The Affordable Housing trigger excerpt ('and 18 Affordable Housing Statement Policies ED3, QP5, TR7 and IF6.') carries the Marketing Exercise policy references. The real trigger (BLP HO3) is a net gain of 10 or more units or over 1,000 sqm of residential floorspace, or 5-9 dwellings in designated rural areas. It applies to outline and full applications, but Grokbot puts it under Full only.
issues.evidence: Affordable Housing Statement - Driver BLP Policy HO3; application types 'Outline and full applications'.

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment excerpt is actually the Site Levels trigger ('where operational development is proposed which would change land levels, and for all basement and swimming pool proposals'). FRA is a national requirement with Flood Zone triggers.
issues.evidence: Site Levels and Finished Floor Levels item; FRA is in the National Validation Requirements table.

issues.detail: Several excerpts merge neighbouring items. Health Impact Assessment is mixed with lighting and heritage text; the actual trigger is major developments. Lighting Assessment carries a misplaced heritage bullet; the actual trigger is new or replacement external lighting, excluding advertisement consent. Housing mix (M4(2)/M4(3)) is mixed with Site Connectivity and telecoms text; the actual trigger is all applications for 20 or more dwellings. Statement of Community Involvement reads 'Statement of 31 Utilities Assessment'; the source item 'Site Connectivity Plan - Communications' requires a Statement of Community Engagement, typically for majors.

The Self-build excerpt is the Phasing Plan trigger ('Any self build development of more than one unit') merged with the Planning Statement trigger. The Self/Custom Build Statement applies to any application that includes a self or custom build element and must follow the RBWM Self Build Guidance Note.
issues.evidence: Self/Custom Build Statement - Driver BLP HO1/HO2.

issues.detail: The 'Schedule of works (listed building)' row holds arboricultural document text ('Assessment, Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan'). The row is mislabelled and has no listed-building content.
issues.evidence: Tree Survey, Arboricultural Impact Assessment, Arboricultural Method Statement, Tree Protection Plan item.

issues.detail: The pre-application advice tab items and the 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' Full planning row are recommendations, not validation requirements. The hard-copy submission rule is process text.
issues.evidence: 'Pre-application advice is strongly recommended...'; 'We recommend that pre-application advice is sought...'

issues.detail: Other excerpts are fragments: Roof plan ('only existing roof plan will be required.'); Heritage Statement ('...should include: 10'); Floor plans ('and Proposed Elevations - Always. and should detail the original size...'); BNG (taken from the S106 Heads of Terms text); LBC Design and Access Statement (merged with the Crown land statement); Householder tree survey (sentences interleaved with page numbers).
issues.evidence: Grokbot trigger_excerpt fields vs PDF items.

issues.detail: Most Full planning rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' although the PDF names application types for each item. Examples: the CIL form is 'Always' but is shown only under Full; Ecology applies to all applications including householder; Affordable housing also applies to Outline.
issues.evidence: Each item in the PDF has an application-types column; CIL Form - 'Always'.

issues.detail: 'Wherever possible, should fit onto A4 or A3 paper' appears twice in tab_items. The Transport Assessment and Travel Plan rows repeat the same excerpt for what is a single combined item in the source.
issues.evidence: Source item 'Transport Assessment and Travel Plan'.

summary: Grokbot's link is correct and current (adopted 5 February 2026), but the date comes from the URL path. The extraction misses most of the local list (about 27 items, including street scene, levels and sections, CEMP, waste strategy, air quality, noise, SuDS, energy, archaeology) and all the non-planning application-type requirements. Many trigger excerpts are taken from the wrong neighbouring item.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
